title: Building a Winning Global Talent Strategy
what_it_is: Building a Winning Global Talent Strategy

sections.label: Singapore ranked second in talent index
sections.summary: INSEAD and the Portulans Institute ranked Singapore second in their Global Talent Attractiveness Index, which recognises bringing in and developing talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just last week, INSEAD and the Portulans Institute ranked Singapore second in their Global Talent Attractiveness Index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Index recognises not only a country’s ability to bring in global talent, but also how well it develops its local talent.

sections.label: Relationship with global talent transactional
sections.summary: The speaker's view is that Singapore's relationship with incoming global talent should be made clear as transactional in the first instance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, my view is that we should make clear that our relationship with global talent coming into Singapore is transactional in the first instance.

sections.label: Testing phase for expatriates and PRs
sections.summary: A testing phase could occur during a work pass or permanent residency, and ICA already considers family ties, contribution and commitment criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This testing phase could occur both while an expatriate is in Singapore on a work pass or during permanent residency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I note that the Immigration and Checkpoint Authority already considers as criteria for Citizenship or Permanent Residency, an applicant’s “family ties to Singapore”, their “ability to contribute to Singapore and integrate into our society” and their “commitment to sinking roots in Singapore”.

sections.label: Youth survey on locals and foreigners
sections.summary: A National Youth Council survey found 17% felt locals and foreigners get along well and 20% felt foreigners integrate comfortably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A National Youth Council survey amongst Singapore youth earlier this year found that only 17% felt that locals and foreigners get along well here despite their differences and only 20% felt that foreigners are able to integrate into local culture comfortably.

sections.label: Employers on Fair Consideration Framework watchlist
sections.summary: The Manpower Minister shared that over 1,700 employers are on the FCF watchlist and 300 companies breached the FCF from 2017 to 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The hon Minister for Manpower shared last month that more than 1,700 employers have been placed on the Fair Consideration Framework’s watchlist for having a high concentration of a single foreign nationality source and that 300 companies have breached the FCF from 2017 to 2021.

sections.label: Compulsory initiation programme for expatriates
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a compulsory initiation programme incorporating three "Respects" for all new expatriates under all pass types, administered by employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To help expatriates ease into Singaporean culture and start our relationship on the right footing, I suggest implementing a compulsory initiation programme that could incorporate these three “Respects” for all new expatriates under all types of passes, to be administered by their employer.

sections.label: Singaporeans and foreigner jobs
sections.summary: Some Singaporeans will lose jobs to foreigners, but policies must ensure foreigners eventually lose jobs to Singaporeans as skills transfer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the midst of this, some Singaporeans will lose jobs to foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But what our policies must ensure is that over time, foreigners will lose jobs to Singaporeans, as we become able to fill these roles ourselves, including by know-how and skills being transferred to us from our expat colleagues.

sections.label: Wong on reclaiming jobs
sections.summary: Lawrence Wong said getting rid of foreigners to reclaim jobs for Singaporeans is flawed because jobs may go overseas instead.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said at the Singapore Economic Policy Forum last month, thinking that we can get simply just get rid of foreigners to “reclaim” jobs for Singaporeans is flawed because these jobs may not automatically go to Singaporeans – they may go overseas, to countries with larger pools of talent.

sections.label: SMEs benefit from diverse experience
sections.summary: Local SMEs and entrepreneurs can benefit from diverse experience mid-level executives bring, citing Kabam Robotics and its co-founders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our local SMEs and entrepreneurs can benefit from the diverse experience that mid-level executives can bring to their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I recently visited Kabam Robotics, a local company, which has three co-founders: two Singaporeans and a US citizen, Mr Michael Sayre.

sections.label: Kabam hiring and SME global talent
sections.summary: Kabam employs 30 Singaporeans and hired foreigners due to limited robotics talent, while building Singaporean expertise through IHL partnerships.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Kabam employs 30 Singaporeans and they have shared with me that they had to shore up their technical team with some foreigners because the talent pool in robotics in Singapore is limited, but that they were working, through extensive partnerships with our IHLs to build up the expertise of their Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to urge SMEs to also look at how they can leverage on global talents to augment their local workforces to build their businesses, to transfer know-how and to build local expertise; and for MOM to recognise that this is a legitimate reason for SMEs to look to hire foreigners.

sections.label: Balancing global and local talent
sections.summary: Singapore must balance global and local talent, with fair MNC hiring, sensitive Government, gracious expatriates and welcoming Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Ultimately, we must strike a balance between bringing in global talent and nurturing and hiring local talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A winning global talent strategy must address both the practical and emotive aspects, because, Sir, Singapore is not a corporation: Singapore is a country, and we are not only workers, but we are also citizens and this is our home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MNCs must make sure that their hiring practices are fair and do not discriminate against Singaporeans or favour foreigners because there are many skilled Singaporean workers right here, who are eager for good jobs and who can perform.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On the emotive side, the Government must be sensitive to and address the fears and concerns of Singaporeans as we see more foreigners coming into Singapore, expatriates must be gracious guests and respect our way of life, and Singaporeans must be welcoming and hospitable hosts.

sections.label: Singapore talent competitiveness ranking
sections.summary: Singapore ranked top in Asia and second in the world in the 2022 INSEAD Global Talent Competitiveness Index.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Singapore ranked top in Asia and second in the world for attracting and developing talent in the recently published 2022 INSEAD Global Talent Competitiveness Index (GTCI).

sections.label: PR and citizenship criteria
sections.summary: PR and citizenship applications are assessed independently, based on family ties, integration ability, economic contributions and commitment to sinking roots in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Applications for Permanent Residency (PR) or Citizenship are assessed independently, and they are based on considerations, including the applicant's family ties to Singapore, their ability to integrate into our society, their economic contributions and commitment to sinking roots in Singapore.

sections.label: S Pass settling-in pilot
sections.summary: MOM plans to pilot a Settling-In Programme for new S Pass holders next year to familiarise them with working in Singapore and encourage interaction with locals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: MOM also plans to pilot a Settling-In Programme for new S Pass holders next year to familiarise them with working in Singapore and to encourage positive interaction with locals within and beyond the workplace.

sections.label: Fair opportunities and employer action
sections.summary: Fair opportunities will be provided at every step, including action against employers who have not hired fairly, possibly suspending their work pass privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: But rest assured we will do our level best to provide the same fair opportunities at every single step of the way.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: This includes taking action against employers who have not hired fairly and may include suspending their work pass privileges.

sections.label: Programmes for local workforce
sections.summary: Programmes for locals in the workforce include iPOST, the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative, the Global Ready Talent Programme and the Singapore Global Executive Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Just as important are also programmes for locals already in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: So, we have the International Posting Programme (iPOST), the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative and the Global Ready Talent Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: And at Budget earlier this year, we also announced the Singapore Global Executive Programme, which we will be sharing more details next month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: We are expanding our collaboration with countries, including New Zealand, Indonesia and France, to facilitate more Singaporeans in going abroad to study and work.

sections.label: Forward Singapore Empower consultations
sections.summary: Under the Empower pillar of Forward Singapore, workers and companies are being consulted on reducing barriers deterring locals from global and regional opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Under the Empower pillar of the Forward Singapore exercise that I am leading, alongside NTUC Secretary-General Ng Chee Meng and Senior Minister of State Dr Koh Poh Koon, we have been and we will continue to be consulting workers and companies on how to reduce barriers, how to remove obstacles that are deterring locals from taking up global and regional opportunities.
